attack_mechanism: RTL connectivity realizes this dependence as `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r4 -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_src -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_out_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.cpu_halt_st -> openMSP430.dbg_0.cpu_stat_rd`. When the debug register-access command selects architectural R4, the register-file read value is routed through `dbg_reg_din` and the debug memory/output muxes. `openMSP430.dbg_0.cpu_stat_rd` is a selected stage of that readback chain; the relevant assignment conditions include `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.src_reg_src_sel`, `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.inst_bw`, `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r2_wr`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.irq_detect`. An adversary with debug-port or internal-probe access can sample `openMSP430.dbg_0.cpu_stat_rd` while the R4 read command is active. The sampled word reveals the complete R4 contents, rather than only a predicate or indirect effect of the register value.

RTL connectivity realizes this dependence as `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r4 -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_src -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_incr_val -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r14`. A register-to-register instruction can select R4 on `reg_src` and write the unchanged or ALU-transformed result into another architectural register. `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r14` stores or forwards that copied value after the destination write edge; the relevant assignment conditions include `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r14_wr`. Reading or probing `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r14` after the transfer provides an alternate observation point even if R4 itself is protected. The attacker obtains the R4 word, or a reversible transform of it, through a less protected register location.
